title: COMP 4736 · Part 1
subtitle: Introduction: multilevel machines, the OS as extended machine and resource manager, kernel and user mode, the CPU and pipelining, memory, registers and cache, disks, I/O and interrupts, buses, the OS zoo, processes, files and protection
description: Part 1 of Rahim Oraji's lectures (Tanenbaum Ch. 1 and lecture notes), the largest deck and more than half of the practice midterm: the six-level machine from digital logic to high-level language, the OS as software, extended machine and resource manager, kernel versus user mode and the four x86 rings, the CPU's ALU (the B − A example in 8 bits), control unit and fetch-decode-execute, RISC against CISC, pipelining with the car factory (cycle time 2 h, latency 6 h) and superscalar CPUs, multithreading, multicore, multiprocessors and multicomputers, the memory hierarchy, PC, stack pointer and PSW, EFLAGS, cache lines and sets (64 KB ÷ 64 B = 1024 lines, 128 sets), direct mapping CI = MI % lines and the slide's 15-request trace, replacement algorithms, RAM organizations, disks (seek, rotation, transfer rates) and SSDs, device controllers and drivers, busy waiting, interrupts and DMA, the buses, the nine-entry OS zoo, processes, files, i-nodes, mount, pipes and the rwx protection bits. Playback animations for the pipeline, the cache trace and the interrupt; an ALU and an rwx widget. Ends with a mock midterm section and the closed-book recall drill.
intro:
:::quiz Midterm weight
On the instructor's practice paper 42 of the 74 Part 1 marks and two of the five written questions (a pipeline's instructions per second and delay; a direct-mapped cache trace) come from this Part. The T/F items are slide sentences with one word changed ("Operating systems turn ugly software into beautiful abstractions" is False; "Registers are used just only in CPUs" is False). Closed book: every list, ring number and figure must come from memory.
:::
